recipes.name: Fond Blanc de Volaille (White Chicken Stock)
recipes.flavorProfile: A clear, pale, gently savory stock that tastes of chicken and sweet vegetables without any browned notes.
recipes.healthBenefit: A light stock that carries some protein and gelatin from the bones and minerals from the vegetables, with no added salt so the dish it goes into sets the seasoning.

ingredients.baseName: Chicken, broiler, back, meat and skin

ingredients.cutPrep: peeled and halved, one half studded with a clove
a few sprigs, in the bouquet garni

instructions: Rinse the chicken carcasses and wings under cold water and put them in a large pot.
Cover with the cold water and bring slowly to a simmer over medium heat, 20 to 30 minutes, skimming off the grey foam as it rises.
Add the carrot, the onion studded with the clove, the leek, celery, garlic, the bouquet garni of thyme, bay and parsley stalks, the peppercorns and the white wine.
Keep at a bare simmer, never a boil, for 1 hour 30 minutes to 2 hours, skimming now and then. Do not salt.
Strain through a fine sieve lined with damp muslin without pressing the solids, cool quickly, and lift off the fat once cold. Keep 2 to 3 days in the fridge or freeze.

nutritionHighlights.note: A little, from the chicken bones and skin, mostly as gelatin.
From the carrot, leek and celery.

citations.source: Meilleur du Chef, Fond blanc de volaille
Guide Michelin, Révision des bases : préparer un fond blanc

recipes.curationNote: Guide Michelin, Révision des bases : préparer un fond blanc for every amount and step; 750 g to 1 kg bones for 1.5 L, carrot, 1 celery branch, 1 garlic clove, onion studded with 1 clove, leek white, bouquet garni, some pepper; white wine from Meilleur du Chef.

recipes.name: Fond Brun de Veau (Brown Veal Stock)
recipes.flavorProfile: Deep, roasted and meaty, with the sweetness of browned vegetables and a body that coats the tongue from the bones.
recipes.healthBenefit: A rich-tasting but lean stock that brings gelatin from the veal bones and a little potassium from the vegetables, with no salt added.

ingredients.prepNote: 1000 g veal bones (knuckle and marrow bones) simmered in 2000 ml water, counted as 2000 g home-made beef stock (1 g per ml); the bones themselves are not eaten

ingredients.cutPrep: a few sprigs, in the bouquet garni

instructions: Heat the oven to 480°F (250°C). Spread the veal bones in a roasting tin and roast for 15 to 30 minutes, turning once, until well browned.
Add the carrot, onion and garlic to the tin and roast 10 to 15 minutes more, then stir in the tomato paste and give it 3 to 5 minutes.
Tip everything into a stockpot, pour off the fat, and deglaze the tin with a little of the water, scraping the brown bits into the pot.
Add the rest of the cold water and the bouquet garni of thyme, bay and parsley stalks. Bring to a simmer and skim.
Simmer very gently, uncovered, for 5 to 6 hours, skimming and topping up with a little water if the bones show. Do not salt.
Strain through a fine sieve without pressing, cool fast and lift off the fat. Keep up to 48 hours in the fridge, or freeze.

nutritionHighlights.note: Mostly gelatin drawn from the roasted veal bones.

citations.source: Meilleur du Chef, Fond brun de veau
Wikipédia, Demi-glace (fond brun and espagnole in the classic sauce system)

recipes.curationNote: Meilleur du Chef gives 1 kg bones, 100 g carrot, 50 g onion, 2 garlic cloves, 1 tbsp tomato paste, 2 L water for 1 L, roasting at 250°C. 4 servings of 1 cup. Veal bones are not in the database.

recipes.name: Fumet de Poisson (Fish Stock)
recipes.flavorProfile: Light, clean and briny, with white wine and shallot sweetness behind the taste of the sea.
recipes.healthBenefit: A quick, lean stock that carries minerals and a little protein from the fish bones, made without salt.

ingredients.prepNote: 500 g white fish bones and heads (sole, turbot, whiting), gills removed simmered in 600 ml water, counted as 600 g home-made fish stock (1 g per ml); the bones themselves are not eaten

ingredients.cutPrep: a few sprigs, in the bouquet garni

instructions: Soak the fish bones and heads in cold water for 10 to 15 minutes to draw out the blood, then drain.
Melt the butter in a wide pan and sweat the carrot, onion, shallot and leek over low heat without colour, 4 to 5 minutes.
Add the bones and stir for 3 to 4 minutes until they turn opaque.
Pour in the white wine and let it bubble for 1 to 2 minutes, then add the cold water and the bouquet garni.
Bring to a simmer, skim, and cook gently for 20 to 25 minutes, no longer, or the stock turns bitter. Do not salt.
Strain through a fine sieve and cool quickly. Keep 1 to 2 days in the fridge or freeze.

nutritionHighlights.note: Some, from the white fish bones and heads.

citations.source: Meilleur du Chef, Fumet de poisson

recipes.curationNote: Meilleur du Chef: 500 g bones, 300 ml white wine, 50 g carrot, 80 g onion, 30 g shallot, 1 leek, 50 g butter, 600 ml water, 20 to 25 minutes, about 1 L. 4 servings of 1 cup.

recipes.name: Court-Bouillon
recipes.flavorProfile: A fragrant, lightly herbal poaching liquid with the sweetness of carrot and shallot and a dry vermouth lift.
recipes.healthBenefit: Fish and shellfish poached in it need no fat, and it is mostly water with a little flavour from the vegetables and herbs.

ingredients.cutPrep: a few sprigs, in the bouquet garni

instructions: Put the water, carrot, shallots, celery, vermouth, thyme, bay, parsley stalks and peppercorns in a wide pan.
Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer for 10 to 15 minutes so the vegetables give up their flavor.
Lower the fish or shellfish into the barely trembling liquid and poach 3 to 5 minutes for fillets, longer for a whole fish, without letting it boil.
Strain and keep the liquid if it is wanted for a sauce.
recipes.curationNote: Chef Simon, Poisson au court-bouillon for every amount and step; 60 cl water, 2 carrots, 3 shallots, 10 cl Noilly Prat, thyme, 1 bay leaf, parsley stalks, 2 celery stalks, a few peppercorns; no salt.

recipes.name: Sauce Béchamel
recipes.flavorProfile: Smooth, creamy and mild, with the soft warmth of nutmeg and a gentle pinch of cayenne.
recipes.healthBenefit: Milk brings calcium and protein; with butter and flour it is a rich sauce best used in measured amounts.

ingredients.baseName: Wheat flour, white, all-purpose, enriched, unbleached
Milk, whole, 3.25% milkfat, with added vitamin D

instructions: Bring the milk to a boil in one pan.
Melt the butter in a heavy saucepan, add the flour and stir over low heat for 2 to 3 minutes to cook a white roux that does not colour.
Take the roux off the heat and pour on the boiling milk all at once, whisking hard so no lumps form.
Return to the heat and bring to a boil, whisking, then simmer gently for 5 to 10 minutes, stirring the bottom so it does not catch.
Season with salt, cayenne and nutmeg. Press cling film on the surface if it is not used at once.
recipes.curationNote: Meilleur du Chef: 70 g butter, 70 g flour, 1 L milk, salt, cayenne, nutmeg. About 1 L, 16 servings of 1/4 cup. The white roux is made in the same pan, so it is written in rather than linked to Roux Blond.

components.note: 700 ml, boiling; use Fumet de Poisson for a fish velouté

recipes.name: Sauce Velouté
recipes.flavorProfile: Silky and savory, tasting of the pale stock it is made from, lighter than a béchamel.
recipes.healthBenefit: Made with stock rather than milk, it is lighter than a cream sauce and carries a little protein from the stock.
instructions: Warm the blond roux in a heavy saucepan over low heat.
Pour in the boiling stock a ladle at a time, whisking until smooth after each.
Bring to a boil, whisking, then lower the heat and simmer gently for 20 to 30 minutes, skimming the skin that forms, until it coats a spoon.
Season lightly with salt and white pepper and strain through a fine sieve.

nutritionHighlights.note: A little, from the chicken stock.

recipes.curationNote: Meilleur du Chef: 30 g butter, 30 g flour (a blond roux) and 700 ml stock, cooked 30 minutes, for 500 ml. 8 servings of 1/4 cup. Roux Blond makes 8 servings of about 14 g, so 60 g is 4; Fond Blanc makes 6 cups, so 700 ml is about 3.

components.note: 60 g, cooked on to a light brown

recipes.name: Sauce Espagnole
recipes.flavorProfile: Dark, glossy and deeply savory, with roasted veal, smoky salt pork and a round tomato sweetness.
recipes.healthBenefit: A concentrated brown sauce used in small amounts, bringing savory depth for very little fat.

ingredients.cutPrep: a few sprigs, in the bouquet garni

instructions: Brown the lardons in a heavy pan for 4 to 5 minutes, add the carrot and onion and colour them lightly, 5 to 8 minutes.
Pour off the fat, add the white wine and reduce it by half, 2 to 3 minutes.
Cook the roux on low heat until it turns light brown, 3 to 5 minutes, then whisk in the hot brown stock a little at a time.
Add the browned vegetables and lardons, the thyme and bay. Simmer very gently for 1 hour 45 minutes to 2 hours, skimming often.
Strain, return to the pan, add the tomato paste and fresh tomatoes and simmer 45 minutes to 1 hour more, skimming, until reduced to about 500 ml.
Strain once more through a fine sieve. Keep 3 to 4 days in the fridge.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the tomatoes and tomato paste.
A little, from the veal stock and lardons.

recipes.curationNote: Meilleur du Chef: 1 L brown veal stock, 60 g roux, carrot, onion, 50 g salted lardons, half a glass of white wine, thyme, half a bay leaf, 100 ml tomato concentrate, 3 tomatoes, about 500 ml. The roux is the house Roux Blond taken a little further. 8 servings of 1/4 cup.

recipes.name: Demi-Glace
recipes.flavorProfile: Intense, glossy and almost sticky, a spoonful of concentrated roasted veal and wine.
recipes.healthBenefit: Used by the spoonful, it adds a great deal of savory depth to a sauce for very little fat.
instructions: Put the espagnole and the brown veal stock in a heavy saucepan and bring to a simmer.
Reduce gently, skimming often, for 45 minutes to 1 hour 15 minutes, until the volume has dropped by more than half and the sauce coats a spoon.
Off the heat, stir in the Madeira if using, then strain through a fine sieve.
Cool and keep 4 to 5 days in the fridge, or freeze in small portions.

nutritionHighlights.note: A little, mostly gelatin from the veal stock.

recipes.curationNote: Wikipédia gives the classic Escoffier route: equal parts espagnole and fond brun reduced by more than half until nappant, finished with Madeira. Meilleur du Chef describes the same reduction by half. 500 ml in gives about 240 ml, 8 servings of 2 tbsp (30 ml). Espagnole serving is 1/4 cup, so 250 ml is 4; fond brun 1 cup, so 1.

recipes.name: Sauce Tomate (French Tomato Sauce)
recipes.flavorProfile: A smooth, savory tomato sauce rounded with salt pork and slowly cooked vegetables, deeper and less sharp than a quick tomato sauce.
recipes.healthBenefit: Tomato paste and slow cooking bring lycopene, and the carrots add vitamin A.

ingredients.baseName: Wheat flour, white, all-purpose, enriched, unbleached

ingredients.cutPrep: a few sprigs, in the bouquet garni

instructions: Heat the oven to 300°F (150°C).
Melt the butter in a flameproof casserole and brown the diced pork belly for 4 to 5 minutes.
Add the carrot, onion and garlic and colour lightly, 5 to 8 minutes. Sprinkle on the flour and stir for 2 to 3 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste, then the hot water, a bouquet garni of the thyme, bay leaf and parsley stalks, salt, pepper and a pinch of sugar. Bring to a boil.
Cover and cook in the oven for 1 hour 30 minutes to 2 hours.
Strain through a fine sieve, pressing the vegetables, and check the seasoning.
recipes.curationNote: Meilleur du Chef, Sauce tomate for every amount and step; 200 ml concentrate, 50 g butter, 150 g salted pork belly, 160 g carrot, 160 g onion, 4 garlic cloves, 50 g flour, bouquet garni, 1.5 L water; salt and pepper with no amount, sugar a pinch (the author says 3 to 4 pinches); same quantity as ours.

components.note: about 240 g, warm, from 300 g butter

recipes.name: Sauce Hollandaise
recipes.flavorProfile: Warm, buttery and airy, with a bright edge of lemon and a faint heat from the piment.
recipes.healthBenefit: A rich butter and egg sauce, a treat, though the yolks bring vitamin A and choline.
instructions: Whisk the yolks with the cold water in a heavy saucepan or a bowl set over barely simmering water.
Keep whisking over gentle heat until the mixture is pale, thick and foamy and reaches 149°F (65°C), 5 to 8 minutes. Do not let it go hotter or the yolks scramble.
Off the heat, pour in the warm clarified butter in a thin stream, whisking all the time, until thick and glossy.
Season with the lemon juice, salt and a pinch of piment d'Espelette. Keep warm, not hot, over a bain-marie and use within 1 hour.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the egg yolks and butter.

recipes.curationNote: Meilleur du Chef, Sauce hollandaise for every amount and step; 300 g butter, 5 yolks, 1 tbsp water per yolk, juice of half a lemon, salt with no amount, a pinch of piment d'Espelette; same quantity as ours.

components.note: about 240 g, warm, from 300 g butter

recipes.name: Sauce Béarnaise
recipes.flavorProfile: Rich and buttery like a hollandaise, sharpened with a shallot and vinegar reduction and fresh tarragon.
recipes.healthBenefit: A rich sauce for a steak or fish, a treat in small amounts; the yolks bring vitamin A and choline.

ingredients.cutPrep: about 2 tbsp chopped, half for the reduction, half to finish

instructions: Put the vinegar, shallots, crushed peppercorns and half the tarragon in a small heavy pan and reduce over low heat to about a quarter, 5 to 8 minutes. Let it cool a little.
Add the yolks and the cold water and whisk over very gentle heat until thick and foamy and at 149°F (65°C), 5 to 8 minutes.
Off the heat, whisk in the warm clarified butter in a thin stream until thick.
Strain if you like a smooth sauce, then stir in the rest of the tarragon and the chervil and season with salt and cayenne. Keep warm in a bain-marie and use within 1 hour.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the egg yolks and butter.

recipes.curationNote: Meilleur du Chef, Sauce béarnaise for every amount and step; 300 g butter, 5 yolks, 100 ml spirit vinegar, 50 g shallots, 5 g peppercorns, 2 tbsp tarragon, a pinch of chervil, salt and cayenne with no amount; same quantity as ours.

recipes.name: Beurre Blanc
recipes.flavorProfile: Pale, creamy and tangy, a warm emulsion of butter with sharp shallot, white wine and lemon.
recipes.healthBenefit: Almost all butter, so it is a rich sauce for fish served by the spoonful.
instructions: Put the shallot, white wine and lemon juice in a small heavy pan and reduce over medium heat until almost dry, 5 to 8 minutes.
Add the cold water and lower the heat to the minimum.
Whisk in the cold butter a few cubes at a time, adding more only as each melts into a creamy sauce. Never let it boil.
Season with salt and pepper, strain if you want it smooth, and keep warm over a bain-marie for up to 30 minutes.
recipes.curationNote: Meilleur du Chef, Beurre blanc for every amount and step; 80 g butter, 7 cl wine, 1 lemon, 1 shallot, 2 to 3 tbsp water, salt and pepper to taste; same batch as ours.

recipes.name: Sauce Mornay
recipes.flavorProfile: A creamy béchamel turned nutty and savory with melted Gruyère, enriched with an egg yolk.
recipes.healthBenefit: Milk and Gruyère bring calcium and protein; it is a rich sauce for gratins.
instructions: Bring the béchamel back to a simmer, whisking.
Off the heat, whisk in the egg yolk, then the grated Gruyère until melted and smooth.
Season with salt, pepper and a little nutmeg. Use at once to coat a gratin, or press cling film on the surface to keep it warm for up to 30 minutes.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the milk, cheese and yolk.

recipes.curationNote: Meilleur du Chef builds it on a béchamel of 40 g butter, 40 g flour, 500 ml milk, then 50 g Gruyère or Emmental and 1 yolk. Linked to the house béchamel (16 servings per litre, so 500 ml is 8). About 550 ml, 9 servings of 1/4 cup.

recipes.name: Pâte Brisée (Shortcrust)
recipes.flavorProfile: A crisp, buttery, lightly salted crust that snaps cleanly and stays neutral enough for a savory or a sweet filling.
recipes.healthBenefit: A pastry made from flour and butter, so it is energy dense and best thought of as the shell that carries a filling rather than a food in itself.

ingredients.baseName: Wheat flour, white, all-purpose, enriched, unbleached

instructions: Put the flour and salt in a bowl, add the cold butter cubes and rub them in with your fingertips for 2 to 3 minutes until the mix looks like coarse sand.
Make a well, add the beaten egg and most of the cold water, and bring it together with a scraper, adding the rest of the water only if it stays dry.
Press the dough into a ball without kneading, flatten it into a disc, wrap it and chill for 30 minutes to 1 hour.
Roll it out 3 to 4 mm thick on a floured surface, line a 9 to 10 inch (24 to 26 cm) tart tin without stretching the dough, prick the base and chill again for 20 to 30 minutes.
To blind bake, line with parchment and dried beans and bake at 350°F to 400°F (180°C to 200°C) for 15 to 20 minutes, then remove the beans and bake 5 to 10 minutes more until pale gold.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the butter, which is what makes the crust short.

citations.source: Wikilivres, Livre de cuisine : Pâte brisée

recipes.curationNote: Meilleur du Chef, Pâte brisée for every amount and step; 200 g flour, 100 g butter, 1 egg, 50 to 65 g water, a pinch of salt; same quantity as ours.

recipes.name: Pâte Sucrée (Sweet Tart Pastry)
recipes.flavorProfile: A sweet, fine, biscuit-like crust that melts a little on the tongue and tastes of butter and vanilla.
recipes.healthBenefit: A sweet pastry rich in butter and sugar, so it belongs to the treat end of a meal.

ingredients.baseName: Wheat flour, white, all-purpose, enriched, unbleached

instructions: Beat the soft butter with the icing sugar and salt for 1 to 2 minutes until smooth, then beat in the egg and vanilla.
Add the flour all at once and mix only until the dough comes together, without working it.
Flatten into a disc, wrap and chill for at least 1 hour, or up to 2 days.
Roll it 3 mm thick between two sheets of parchment, line a 9 to 10 inch (24 to 26 cm) tart ring and chill 20 to 30 minutes.
Blind bake at 325°F to 340°F (160°C to 170°C) for 10 to 15 minutes for a part-baked case, or 20 to 25 minutes for a fully baked one, until evenly golden.

citations.source: Wikilivres, Livre de cuisine : Pâte brisée (sweet version)

recipes.curationNote: Meilleur du Chef, Pâte sucrée for every amount and step; 200 g flour, 100 g butter, 80 g icing sugar, a pinch of salt, 1 egg, vanilla with no amount; same quantity as ours.

recipes.name: Pâte Feuilletée (Puff Pastry)
recipes.flavorProfile: Hundreds of thin, crackling, buttery layers that shatter when bitten and puff high in the oven.
recipes.healthBenefit: Made of flour, water and a great deal of butter, so it is rich and energy dense and a small portion goes a long way.

ingredients.baseName: Wheat flour, white, all-purpose, enriched, unbleached

ingredients.cutPrep: cold, for the beurre de tourage

instructions: Mix the flour, salt and cold water into a smooth dough (the détrempe), shape it into a ball, cut a cross in the top, wrap and chill for 1 to 2 hours.
Beat the cold butter between two sheets of parchment into a flat square about 1/2 inch (1 cm) thick that is as supple as the dough.
Roll the dough into a cross shape, set the butter square in the middle and fold the four flaps over it to enclose it completely.
Roll the block into a long rectangle, fold it in three like a letter and turn it a quarter turn: that is one turn. Give a second turn, then chill for 30 minutes to 1 hour.
Repeat until you have given six turns in all, two at a time with a rest in the fridge between each pair. Chill at least 1 hour before rolling and baking at 400°F to 430°F (200°C to 220°C).

nutritionHighlights.note: From the large share of butter folded through the layers.

recipes.curationNote: Meilleur du Chef: 500 g flour, 250 g water, 10 g salt, 375 g butter, about 1.1 kg, six turns. Wikipédia confirms détrempe plus beurre de tourage and the classic six turns. 20 servings of about 55 g.

recipes.name: Pâte à Choux
recipes.flavorProfile: Light, hollow, crisp-shelled puffs with a soft, eggy inside that take any sweet or savory filling.
recipes.healthBenefit: Mostly egg and flour, so each small puff brings a little protein along with the butter.

ingredients.baseName: Milk, whole, 3.25% milkfat, with added vitamin D
Wheat flour, white, all-purpose, enriched, unbleached

instructions: Bring the milk, water, butter and salt to a full boil in a saucepan so the butter melts completely.
Take the pan off the heat, tip in all the flour at once and beat hard with a wooden spoon until smooth.
Put the pan back over medium heat and stir for 2 to 4 minutes to dry the paste, until it pulls away from the sides and leaves a thin film on the base.
Move the paste to a bowl, let it cool for 3 to 5 minutes, then beat in the eggs a little at a time until the dough is glossy and falls from the spoon in a thick ribbon.
Pipe small mounds on a lined tray and bake at 340°F to 360°F (170°C to 180°C) for 25 to 35 minutes without opening the oven, until puffed, golden and light.

citations.source: Meilleur du Chef, Pâte à choux

recipes.curationNote: Meilleur du Chef, Pâte à choux for every amount and step; 125 g milk, 125 g water, 165 g flour, 100 g butter, a pinch of salt, 250 g eggs; same quantity as ours.

recipes.name: Pâte à Crêpes (Crêpe Batter)
recipes.flavorProfile: Thin, tender, lacy-edged pancakes that taste of egg, milk and browned butter.
recipes.healthBenefit: A light batter of milk, egg and flour that brings some protein and calcium, and stays modest when filled simply.

ingredients.baseName: Wheat flour, white, all-purpose, enriched, unbleached
Milk, whole, 3.25% milkfat, with added vitamin D

instructions: Put the flour and salt in a bowl, make a well, add the eggs and whisk from the middle outward to a thick, smooth paste.
Whisk in the cold milk a little at a time to keep it free of lumps, then the water, the melted butter and the rum.
Cover and rest the batter in the fridge for at least 1 hour, or overnight.
Heat a lightly buttered crêpe pan over medium high heat, pour in a small ladle of batter and swirl it thin over the base.
Cook 1 to 2 minutes until the edges lift and the underside is golden, flip and cook 30 seconds to 1 minute more. Stack under a cloth.

citations.source: Meilleur du Chef, Pâte à crêpes

recipes.curationNote: Meilleur du Chef, Pâte à crêpes for every amount and step; 125 g flour, 30 g butter, a pinch of salt, optional sugar with no amount, 3 eggs, 300 ml milk, 2 tbsp water, 2 tsp rum; about 12 crêpes, same as ours.

recipes.name: Crème Pâtissière (Pastry Cream)
recipes.flavorProfile: A thick, smooth, vanilla custard that holds its shape and tastes of egg yolk and warm milk.
recipes.healthBenefit: Brings protein and calcium from the milk and eggs, along with a fair amount of sugar, so it is a filling for treats.

ingredients.baseName: Milk, whole, 3.25% milkfat, with added vitamin D

ingredients.prepNote: about 1 tbsp; or the seeds of 1 vanilla pod, as the method describes

ingredients.baseName: Wheat flour, white, all-purpose, enriched, unbleached

instructions: Bring the milk to a simmer with the split vanilla pod and its seeds, then take it off the heat and leave it to infuse for 10 to 15 minutes.
Whisk the yolks, whole eggs and sugar in a bowl for 1 to 2 minutes until pale, then whisk in the flour.
Lift out the vanilla pod and pour half of the hot milk onto the egg mixture, whisking, then pour it all back into the pan.
Cook over medium heat, whisking constantly and scraping the base, until it thickens and bubbles, then keep cooking and whisking for 4 to 5 minutes more so the flour loses its raw taste.
Pour into a shallow dish, press plastic film onto the surface, cool quickly and chill for at least 2 hours. Keep 2 to 3 days in the fridge.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the egg yolks, eggs and milk.

recipes.curationNote: Meilleur du Chef: 1 L milk, 250 g sugar, 100 g flour T55, 6 yolks, 2 eggs, 1 vanilla pod, cook 4 to 5 min after thickening. Wikipédia agrees on milk, yolks or eggs, sugar, flour or starch, vanilla infusion and covering the surface. About 1.1 kg, 16 servings of 1/4 cup.

recipes.name: Crème Anglaise
recipes.flavorProfile: A pourable, silky vanilla custard sauce, sweet and eggy, served cold over cakes, fruit and îles flottantes.
recipes.healthBenefit: Brings protein from the yolks and calcium from the milk with added sugar, so a spoonful is a treat rather than a staple.

ingredients.baseName: Milk, whole, 3.25% milkfat, with added vitamin D

ingredients.prepNote: about 1 tbsp; or the seeds of 1 vanilla pod, as the method describes

instructions: Bring the milk to a simmer with the split vanilla pod and its seeds, then take it off the heat and infuse for 10 to 15 minutes.
Whisk the yolks and sugar for 1 to 2 minutes until pale, then pour on the hot milk a little at a time, whisking.
Return to the pan over low heat and stir constantly with a wooden spoon in a figure of eight, without letting it boil, for 5 to 10 minutes.
Stop when it reaches 180°F to 183°F (82°C to 84°C) and coats the spoon so that a finger drawn across it leaves a clean line (à la nappe).
Strain at once into a cold bowl, stir now and then as it cools, then chill for at least 2 hours. Keep 1 to 2 days in the fridge.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the egg yolks and milk.

recipes.curationNote: Meilleur du Chef: 1 L milk, 8 to 10 yolks, 150 g sugar, 1 vanilla pod, cook to 82°C à la nappe and strain. Wikipédia: milk, fresh yolks, sugar, vanilla, cook between 82 and 84°C or it turns lumpy. 9 yolks is the middle of the range. 16 servings of 1/4 cup.

recipes.name: Roux Blond
recipes.flavorProfile: A pale golden paste of butter and flour that smells of toasted hazelnut and thickens a sauce without tasting of raw flour.
recipes.healthBenefit: Only butter and flour, so it adds a little energy to the sauce it thickens and nothing more.

ingredients.baseName: Wheat flour, white, all-purpose, enriched, unbleached

instructions: Melt the butter in a heavy saucepan over low to medium heat until it foams.
Add the flour all at once and stir with a wooden spoon or whisk into a smooth paste.
Keep stirring over low heat for 3 to 5 minutes, until the roux turns a light straw gold and smells of hazelnut; stop at 1 to 2 minutes for a roux blanc, or carry on 8 to 10 minutes for a roux brun.
Use it at once, whisking in cold or warm liquid gradually, or cool it and keep it covered in the fridge for up to 1 week.

citations.source: Croq-Kilos, Comment faire un roux en cuisine

recipes.curationNote: Croq-Kilos: equal weights butter and flour, blanc 1 to 2 min, blond 3 to 5 min, brun 8 to 10 min. Wikipédia: three roux by cooking time, blond with a hazelnut taste, Curnonsky 80 g butter to 75 g flour per litre. 120 g of roux in 8 servings of 1 tbsp (about 15 g); velouté and espagnole in this file use 4 servings for 1 L.

recipes.name: Duxelles
recipes.flavorProfile: A dark, dry, intensely savory hash of mushrooms and shallot, earthy and buttery, used to stuff, spread and flavor.
recipes.healthBenefit: Mostly mushrooms, which bring B vitamins, potassium and some fiber, cooked in a modest amount of butter.
instructions: Squeeze the chopped mushrooms in a clean cloth, a handful at a time, to press out as much liquid as you can.
Melt the butter in a wide pan over medium heat and soften the shallot and onion for 3 to 5 minutes without browning.
Add the mushrooms, turn the heat up and cook uncovered, stirring often, for 10 to 15 minutes, until all the moisture has gone and the mixture is dry and starting to stick.
Season with salt, pepper and nutmeg, stir in the parsley and take off the heat.
Cool and keep covered in the fridge for 3 to 4 days, or freeze in small portions.

nutritionHighlights.note: Riboflavin and niacin from the mushrooms.

citations.source: Aftouch Cuisine, La duxelles de champignons

recipes.curationNote: Aftouch Cuisine, La duxelles de champignons for every amount and step; 500 g mushrooms, onions, shallots, 50 g butter, salt, pepper, nutmeg to taste; parsley from Escoffier's duxelles on Wikipédia; cream left out as ours is the dry base.

recipes.name: Beurre Clarifié (Clarified Butter)
recipes.flavorProfile: Clear, golden, pure-tasting butter fat that can take high heat without burning and gives a clean butter flavor.
recipes.healthBenefit: Almost all fat once the milk solids and water are gone, so it is used in small amounts; removing the solids also takes out most of the lactose and casein.
instructions: Melt the butter in a small heavy saucepan over very low heat, without stirring, for 10 to 15 minutes.
Skim off the white foam that rises to the top with a spoon.
Pour the clear yellow butter off slowly into a jar, leaving the milky whey at the bottom of the pan behind, or strain it through muslin.

recipes.name: Bisque de Homard

instructions: Split the lobster lengthwise from the head, remove the gravel sac and chop the head and shell into pieces; keep the tail and claws aside.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot over high heat and sear the shell pieces for 3 to 5 minutes, until bright red, then add the tail and claws for 2 to 3 minutes and lift them out.
Lower the heat, add the carrot, celery and shallot to the oil and sweat for 5 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste, then pour in the cognac and let it reduce (or flame it carefully).
Add the white wine and reduce by half, then add the tomatoes, garlic, tarragon, parsley sprigs, rice, fish stock and water.
Simmer gently, covered, for 35 to 40 minutes.

Heat the oil in a wide frying pan and sear the fish, white skin side first.
Turn the fish and finish cooking over low heat. Add a little of the butter and baste the fish with it as it cooks.
Meanwhile, cook the rest of the butter in a small pan until it turns nut brown.
Dip the lemon slices in the parsley and set them on the fish, scattering a little parsley over too.
Pour the lemon juice over the fish, then the beurre noisette, which will foam at once. Serve straight away.

nutritionHighlights.note: Sole is a lean source of protein.
White fish such as sole supplies selenium.

recipes.name: Moules Marinières
recipes.flavorProfile: Sweet, briny mussels steamed open in white wine, shallot and butter, with a broth worth mopping up.
recipes.healthBenefit: Mussels are one of the richest common sources of vitamin B12 and iron, and they are farmed on ropes with no feed added.

ingredients.cutPrep: in the shell, scrubbed and debearded, any open ones that do not close discarded

instructions: Melt the butter in a large pot with a spoonful of water and soften the shallots for 2 to 3 minutes without letting them colour.

Tip in the mussels, pour in the white wine and add half the parsley. Bring to a boil, cover tightly and cook over low heat, shaking the pot once or twice, until the shells have opened, under 10 minutes.
Lift the mussels into warm bowls with a slotted spoon, throwing away any that stayed shut.
Strain the broth back into the pot, stir in the crème fraîche and the pepper and bring it just to a boil. Taste before adding any salt, since the mussels are salty, and pour it over the mussels.
Scatter over the rest of the parsley and serve with bread or fries.

nutritionHighlights.note: Mussels are very high in vitamin B12.
Mussels supply a good amount of iron.

recipes.name: Coquilles Saint-Jacques
recipes.flavorProfile: Sweet, tender scallops seared golden in butter and tossed in garlic and parsley.
recipes.healthBenefit: Scallops are almost pure lean protein and supply vitamin B12 and selenium.

ingredients.cutPrep: shelled, coral removed or kept, patted dry

instructions: Rinse the scallops, drain them and pat them very dry with a cloth so they brown rather than steam.
Heat the butter and olive oil in a frying pan over high heat until the butter foams.
Lay in the scallops in one layer and sear them 1 to 2 minutes a side, until golden outside and still just translucent at the centre. Lift them out and keep them warm.
Lower the heat, add two thirds of the persillade to the pan juices and stir for a few seconds only, then take the pan off the heat before the garlic darkens.
Return the scallops to the pan and toss them in the parsley and garlic.
Season with salt and pepper and serve with the rest of the persillade on top.

nutritionHighlights.note: Scallops are a lean source of protein.

recipes.name: Brandade de Morue
recipes.flavorProfile: A creamy, garlicky whip of salt cod, olive oil and warm milk, rich and savoury with a lift of lemon.
recipes.healthBenefit: Salt cod is a lean, dense protein, and soaking it for a day draws out most of the salt it was cured in.

ingredients.cutPrep: soaked 24 to 36 hours in cold water changed every few hours

ingredients.baseName: Milk, whole, 3.25% milkfat, with added vitamin D

instructions: Soak the salt cod in a large bowl of cold water in the fridge for 24 to 36 hours, changing the water every 2 to 3 hours during the day, until a flake no longer tastes very salty.
Bring the court bouillon to a simmer, slide in the drained cod and poach it gently for 8 to 10 minutes. Do not let it boil hard.
Drain the cod, remove all skin and bones and flake it into a food processor or a heavy pan with the garlic.
Warm the milk and olive oil separately until warm to the touch.
Working the cod with the processor or a wooden spoon, add the oil and milk in turn, a little at a time, until the brandade is white, smooth and creamy like a soft mash.
Beat in the lemon zest and juice and season with pepper; salt is rarely needed.
Serve warm with potatoes boiled in their skins or on toasted bread.

nutritionHighlights.note: Salt cod is a concentrated source of protein.
Olive oil makes up most of the fat.
Even well soaked, salt cod carries more sodium than fresh fish.

recipes.name: Truite aux Amandes
recipes.flavorProfile: Mild, sweet trout baked in white wine with herbs under slivered almonds, finished with almonds browned in butter.
recipes.healthBenefit: Trout supplies omega-3 fats and protein, and the almonds add vitamin E and magnesium.

ingredients.cutPrep: 4 whole trout of about 250 g, cleaned
slivered, a third over the fish and two thirds browned in butter

ingredients.prepNote: to taste; the source gives no amount

instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C).
Lay the trout in a baking dish and cover them with a third of the almonds, keeping the rest aside.
Pour the white wine over them, season with salt and pepper and lay the basil and thyme on top.
Bake for 30 minutes.
Near the end, melt the butter in a frying pan and brown the remaining almonds in it.
Pour the cooking juices from the baking dish into the pan, let them bubble for a minute or two, then spoon the almonds and sauce over the trout.

recipes.name: Lotte à l'Armoricaine
recipes.flavorProfile: Firm, sweet monkfish in a deep red sauce of tomato, onion, white wine and cognac, with thyme, bay and a pinch of cayenne.
recipes.healthBenefit: Monkfish is a lean white fish, and the sauce is built on tomatoes, which supply lycopene.

ingredients.cutPrep: tail, skinned, membrane removed, cut in thick medallions

ingredients.baseName: Wheat flour, white, all-purpose, enriched, unbleached

instructions: Cut the monkfish into thick medallions and dust them lightly with the flour.

Heat the butter and olive oil in a heavy casserole and brown the fish lightly, about 2 minutes a side. Off the heat, pour in the cognac and set it alight away from anything that can catch, or let it bubble off for 1 minute. Lift out the fish and keep its juices.

In the same pot soften the onion and garlic for 3 to 4 minutes. Add the tomatoes, tomato paste, wine, cayenne, bay leaf, thyme and the fish juices, bring nearly to a boil and simmer uncovered for about 30 minutes to reduce.
Return the fish and heat it gently for about 10 minutes, until just firm. Stir in the parsley, season with the salt and pepper, take out the bay leaf and thyme, and serve with rice.

nutritionHighlights.note: Monkfish is a lean source of protein.

recipes.name: Raie au Beurre Noir
recipes.flavorProfile: Soft, sweet ribbons of skate under dark nutty butter, sharp with vinegar and capers.
recipes.healthBenefit: Skate is a lean fish; here it is browned in butter and served with a brown butter sauce, so nearly all the fat comes from the butter.

ingredients.cutPrep: 40 g to cook the fish, 60 g for the beurre noir

instructions: Rinse the skate wings well in cold water and pat them dry; a skate that smells of ammonia is not fresh.
Melt 40 g of the butter in a wide frying pan, or two, and brown the wings on both sides until cooked through. Season with salt and pepper.
When the wings are almost done, melt the remaining 60 g of butter in another pan until it turns nut brown. Add the vinegar, which will bubble up, then the capers, and cook 1 minute.
Set the wings on a serving dish, scatter with the parsley and serve the beurre noir in a sauce boat, with white rice or wax beans.

nutritionHighlights.note: Skate is a lean source of protein.
Most of the fat comes from the butter in the sauce.

recipes.name: Quenelles de Brochet
recipes.flavorProfile: Light, soufflé-like dumplings of pike baked in a creamy crayfish sauce until puffed.
recipes.healthBenefit: Pike is a lean freshwater fish, and the quenelles are bound with eggs and a flour panade; the butter and cream make it a rich dish.

ingredients.baseName: Milk, whole, 3.25% milkfat, with added vitamin D

ingredients.prepNote: 50 g for the panade, 100 g melted for the fish

ingredients.baseName: Wheat flour, white, all-purpose, enriched, unbleached

ingredients.prepNote: a pinch for the quenelles and a pinch for the sauce
a pinch for the quenelles and a pinch for the sauce
for the poaching water, poured away

ingredients.name: crayfish butter (beurre d'écrevisse)
ingredients.prepNote: butter pounded with crayfish shells and strained; sold ready made in France

instructions: Make the panade: bring the milk and 50 g of the butter to a boil, take the pan off the heat and tip in the flour all at once. Stir it over low heat until the paste dries and comes away from the sides. Let it cool until lukewarm.

Blend the pike to a fine paste. Add the panade, then the eggs one at a time, then the remaining 100 g of butter, melted, with the nutmeg and a pinch each of salt and pepper. Chill the mixture for 1 hour.
Bring the salted water to a bare simmer. Shape the mixture between two spoons into ovals and poach them a few at a time for about 10 minutes, lifting each out once it floats.
For the Nantua sauce, warm the béchamel and stir in the crayfish butter, then the crème fraîche and the crayfish tails. Season with a pinch of salt and pepper and simmer for a few minutes.
Heat the oven to 350°F (180°C). Lay the quenelles in a gratin dish, cover them with the sauce and bake for 20 minutes, until puffed. Serve straight away.

nutritionHighlights.note: Pike, eggs and crayfish make this a high protein dish.
Butter, crayfish butter and cream carry most of the fat.
The béchamel and the milk in the panade supply calcium.

recipes.name: Saumon en Papillote
recipes.flavorProfile: Moist, tender salmon steamed in a paper parcel on thin strips of carrot, onion and courgette, with lemon juice and zest.
recipes.healthBenefit: Salmon is one of the best food sources of omega-3 fats and vitamin D, and the parcel steams it in its juices with very little fat added.
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F (180°C).
Cut the carrot, onion and courgette into thin strips and cook them gently in a covered pan until tender.
Cut 4 large sheets of baking paper. Divide the vegetables between them, lay a salmon fillet on each and add a little lemon juice, some zest, salt and pepper.
Fold the paper over and seal the parcels tightly so no steam escapes.
Bake 20 to 30 minutes, depending on the thickness of the fillets, and open the parcels at the table.

nutritionHighlights.note: Salmon is rich in EPA and DHA.
Salmon is one of the few foods with a useful amount of vitamin D.

recipes.name: Thon Basquaise
recipes.flavorProfile: Floured, pan-fried tuna simmered in a soft, sweet sauce of red peppers, onion and tomato with a pinch of herbes de Provence.
recipes.healthBenefit: Tuna supplies protein and omega-3 fats, and the pipérade adds a large amount of vitamin C from the peppers.

ingredients.cutPrep: 1 large slice or 4 thick steaks, skinned and boned
1 tbsp for the compote, the rest to sear the tuna

ingredients.baseName: Wheat flour, white, all-purpose, enriched, unbleached

ingredients.cutPrep: a splash, plus more if needed

instructions: Heat 1 tbsp of the olive oil in a frying pan and soften the onions and peppers. Add a splash of water and a little of the salt, cover and stew over low heat.

Heat the rest of the oil in a large frying pan. Coat the tuna with flour on both sides and cook it about 10 minutes, turning once, until golden on both sides. Season with salt, lift it out and keep it warm, leaving the oil in the pan.
Add the chopped tomatoes and garlic to that pan and cook 15 minutes.
Stir in the pepper and onion compote and the herbes de Provence, and season with pepper.
Return the tuna, spoon some of the vegetables over it, cover and simmer gently 15 to 20 minutes, adding a little water if it gets dry.
Serve the tuna with the sauce, with white rice.

nutritionHighlights.note: Tuna is a rich source of protein.
Peppers supply a large amount of vitamin C.
